title: prez's acceptance suite leaves its present decks in TMPDIR, and a pdf whose print fails leaves its staged HTML
body:
## What

On 19 Oct 2026, closing out on hv's "Nix TMPDIR's detritus", cc removed 54 `prez-<pid>-<nanos>.html` files from this Mac's TMPDIR. prez's own `scratch()` (`opt/prez/crate/src/deck.rs:384`) made them, not a test helper, so 0093 did not cover them. hv's "Nix them, please" (vc's decision 42) is the ask, and vc made it cc's on 20 Oct (cc's todo 42), after hv's "Ok, crack on".

## Where, by reading

Two of prez's verbs stage a file under `std::env::temp_dir()`:

- **`present` without `-o`** (`deck.rs:54-63`) stages the deck in TMPDIR and leaves it there on purpose, because the browser is still reading it after prez exits (spec 6). `opt/prez/crate/test/acceptance.sh` runs `present` that way six times a run, under the caller's TMPDIR: AT06 twice (`:443`, `:489`, through a stub browser) and AT20 four times (`:1221`, `:1240`, `:1275`, `:1294`, through a real Chrome). `theme-addressing.sh`'s one `present` (`:183`) is a refusal that fails in `compile()` before anything is staged.
- **`pdf`** (`deck.rs:30-52`) stages its HTML at `scratch("html")` and removes it (`:49`) only once `drive::print_to_pdf` has returned `Ok`. A `write` that fails (`:38`) or a print that fails (`:43`: Chrome could not run, exited non-zero, or wrote no PDF, the three `Err`s of `drive.rs:23-82`) returns through its `?` and leaves the file, in real use as in the suite. The removal is `let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&staged)`, so a removal that fails says nothing. A collapsed PDF is a warning, since `verify_pagination` returns warnings, so AT05 removes its file, and AT05's `--browser /nonexistent` is refused by the finder before anything is staged.

R1 (slot 199, 20 Oct 2026, on main at `323864c4`, whose code is `1ceade68`'s) measured it with TMPDIR an empty directory of the run's own: `acceptance.sh --strict` (passed 16, failed 0, skipped 0) left six `prez-<pid>-<nanos>.html` and nothing else, two made under AT06 and four under AT20, and `theme-addressing.sh --strict` (passed 20) left none.

## Design

cc, 20 Oct 2026, at `1ceade68`. Size: S. It answers vc's three points of 20 Oct: a product owner exists, No Silent Errors, and the suite's TMPDIR. Read and approved by vc, 20 Oct, with four notes, folded in here: the moved test pins every caller's name (point 1), `Drop` writes without `eprintln!` (point 4), the probe's comment follows the TMPDIR (point 5), and the unit test says what it does as root (point 6). After the read, one correction of cc's own, to point 5's reason: macOS Chrome reads `MAC_CHROMIUM_TMPDIR`, not TMPDIR, for its singleton's socket, so the case for moving WORK is Linux's socket, not this Mac's. Then critic-rust and critic-shell read candidate v1 (20 Oct): one CRITICAL (critic-shell: the work directory's `mktemp` went unchecked) and five recommendations, folded into v2 in points 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7. One of them changes an approved point: `pdf`'s scratch stays in TMPDIR (point 3).

1. **One scratch directory, in `artifact`, for both tools.** showreel's `record::Scratch` (`crates/showreel/src/record.rs:139-179`) is the product owner: a private (`0700`) `showreel-<pid>-<n>` directory made in TMPDIR, or in `/tmp` when TMPDIR is longer than `SCRATCH_BASE_MAX` (36 bytes, so the socket Chrome binds in a profile inside it fits `sun_path`), removed by `remove()`, which says when it cannot, and by `Drop` as a backstop. `pdf`'s staging is a second implementation of a temporary place removed after use, so by `artifact`'s own rule (`crates/artifact/src/lib.rs`: a module moves when two tools already implement it) it moves to `artifact::scratch`, with `scratch_base`, `SCRATCH_BASE_MAX` and their test. `Scratch::new` takes its caller as `scratch::Tool`, an enum of the two, `Prez` and `Showreel`, whose `name()` is the directory's prefix, `<tool>-<pid>-<n>`, and the tool's name in the backstop's line (point 4). `SCRATCH_BASE_MAX`'s arithmetic, which allows `showreel-<pid>-<n>` 19 bytes, now depends on that name, so the moved test runs it over `Tool::ALL`, every name a caller can pass (vc's note 1): a third caller adds a variant, and a longer name fails that test rather than Chrome's bind. One `dir_name` spells `<tool>-<pid>-<n>` for `make` and for that test, so the test measures the name a directory really gets, and an exhaustive match beside `Tool::ALL` sends whoever adds a variant to the list (critic-rust). `Tool::chrome_binds_here` says whether the tool gives Chrome the directory as its TMPDIR, as showreel's recording does, and only then does the base fall back to `/tmp` (point 3); `make`'s remedy names the directory it tried, not TMPDIR. showreel's `record.rs` and `video.rs` take it from `artifact` with the same behaviour, and the wrapper's test stays in `record.rs`. prez and showreel already depend on `artifact`, so no manifest moves and `tests/manifest.rs` holds.
2. **`artifact::testing::TempDir` stays test support, and neither wraps the other.** `TempDir` is `$TMPDIR/<prefix>-<pid>-<tag>`, a fixed name per test that empties a leftover of the same name, always in TMPDIR, where 0093's count reads it, and its failure fails the test. `Scratch` is a fresh `<tool>-<pid>-<n>` that may sit in `/tmp`, and its failure is said while the tool goes on. What they share is the removal: `remove_dir_all`, with `NotFound` as success. That becomes one function in `artifact::scratch` that returns the error and that both call, each wording its own message, so the crate holds one removal, and `TempDir`'s `cannot remove the test directory` stays in test support, out of every release binary, as 0093's check found it.
3. **`pdf` stages inside one.** After `compile()` succeeds, so a deck that does not compile makes nothing, `pdf` makes a `Scratch`, writes `deck.html` in it and prints it. The write's and the print's result are held, the scratch is removed, and then the result is returned, so no `?` can step past the removal. `scratch()` stays as `present`'s alone (point 5), since a deck that must outlive prez is the opposite of a scratch directory. `pdf`'s scratch is made in TMPDIR whatever TMPDIR's length, where prez always staged. prez hands Chrome only a file, so the socket rule is not prez's, and v1's `/tmp` would have moved a Mac's staging out of its per-user TMPDIR into the shared `/tmp`, out of reach of a snap-packaged Chromium, which has a `/tmp` of its own (critic-rust). This replaces the `/tmp` of the approved v1.
4. **A failed removal is said (No Silent Errors).** `Scratch::remove` returns the message, naming the directory and the error, and marks the scratch removed, so `Drop` does nothing after it. On `pdf`'s success path the message goes through `report()`, `deck.rs`'s one door for warnings, as `prez: warning: could not remove the temporary directory <dir>: <error>`. The PDF is made, so prez exits 0 and the warning names what to remove. On the two `Err` paths, the write's and the print's, the same warning is reported first and the original `Failure` is returned, so the print's failure stays the exit status and the leftover is still named. `Drop` is the backstop for a path that never reached `remove`: in prez, after point 3, a panic; in showreel, `Chrome::launch` failing (`record.rs:540-541`, which drops the scratch). There it prints the same message on stderr in the tool's name, `<tool>: warning: ...`, in place of `let _ = self.remove()` (`record.rs:177`), because no caller is left to report it. It writes with `writeln!` to `std::io::stderr()` and drops that write's own result, never `eprintln!` (vc's note 2): `eprintln!` panics when its write fails, as when stderr is a pipe whose reader has gone, and a panic inside `Drop` while unwinding aborts the process, which is exactly when this backstop runs; a write to stderr that fails has nowhere left to report. In showreel, a panic between `launch` and `stop` reaches `Chrome`'s own `Drop`, whose `stop(false)` removes the scratch and handed its warnings to nobody; it now writes each as `showreel: <warning>` the same way (critic-rust). The backstop's `<tool>: warning:` is `report()`'s wording in prez; showreel's own printer says `showreel:` without the word, a one-word difference accepted rather than given a second owner. Beside `TempDir`'s line while a test panics, it is the only printer in `artifact`, and it is reached only where the tool's own door cannot be.
5. **`present` is unchanged, and the suite gives it a TMPDIR of its own** (vc's point iii). `present`'s staged deck is spec 6 (`deck.rs:55-61`): in real use it is one file per presentation, left for the browser and aged out by the OS's temp cleaning. `acceptance.sh` exports a TMPDIR inside its own WORK, so every prez, Chrome, node and python it runs writes there, and the EXIT trap that removes WORK removes it. WORK moves to `/tmp` to do it. Linux Chrome reads TMPDIR for its process singleton's socket directory, `<TMPDIR>/.<prefix>.XXXXXX/SingletonSocket`, up to 46 bytes past it for Chromium's prefix (`record.rs:563-569`; macOS Chrome reads `MAC_CHROMIUM_TMPDIR` instead, which the suite does not set), so on Linux a `$WORK/t/` under a long TMPDIR would push that socket past `sun_path`: the failure `record.rs`'s `SCRATCH_BASE_MAX` records on CI's Linux leg, under `video.sh`'s nested TMPDIR. `mktemp -d /tmp/prez-at.XXXXXX` and `$WORK/t/` keep it at 22 bytes on every machine (under this Mac's own TMPDIR it would be 67), and `pdf`'s scratch directory (point 3) is made in TMPDIR, so inside WORK, where check (b) finds it. A `mktemp` that fails stops the suite by name, since an empty WORK would put every path under `/` (critic-shell's CRITICAL). On CI's Ubuntu leg, where TMPDIR is unset, WORK is in `/tmp` already. AT20's probe finds its window by the URL that is new after the second launch (`at20-window-probe.mjs:43-45`), so the move breaks nothing there, but its comment at `:40` names the file as `file:///.../T/prez-<pid>-<nanos>` and becomes `<TMPDIR>/prez-<pid>-<nanos>` (vc's note 4). `theme-addressing.sh` stages nothing and is unchanged.
6. **The checks, red first.** Two in `acceptance.sh`, black-box like every check there, and neither needs a real browser. (a) In AT06, the deck the stub browser was handed, its `--app=file://` argument, is inside the suite's own TMPDIR: red on main, where it lands in the caller's. (b) In AT05, outside its Chrome branch, a `pdf` through a stub browser that records its arguments, and whether the file it was handed existed while it ran, and exits 1: prez fails with the print's failure; the file sat in a scratch directory in the suite's own TMPDIR and existed while the stub ran; and it is gone, with its directory, once prez has exited. A stub that could not be written, or never ran, is named rather than read as a pass (critic-shell). Red on main, where the file sits in TMPDIR itself and stays. (c) In `artifact::scratch`, one unit test that a directory that cannot be removed is named in `remove`'s message, so that path can go red. It makes a `Scratch`, a subdirectory in it holding one file, and takes the subdirectory's write permission away (mode `0500`), so `remove_dir_all` cannot unlink the file; it asserts that `remove` returns a message naming the scratch's directory, then restores the mode and removes the directory itself (vc's note 3). As root a mode does not stop removal, and a test cannot be skipped from inside, so before asserting it tries to write a probe file into the `0500` subdirectory: if that succeeds, the mode does not bind here, and the test fails, saying that it cannot run where a mode does not stop removal (as root), rather than passing. CI's runners and kovacs run as a user, not root. And the count: R1 named what main's suite leaves in an empty TMPDIR (six decks), and R2 shows none after.
7. **Runs**, each booked with utilz-vc. R1 (heavy, main, no candidate; slot 199, done, above): in a clean detached worktree at main's head, `cargo build --release --workspace`, then `acceptance.sh --strict` and `theme-addressing.sh --strict`, each under an empty TMPDIR of the run's own, every file left named with the AT that made it. R2 (heavy, the candidate in `wt-0095`, after vc's read), red first: (R) the new AT05 and AT06 checks against main's binary, R1's build, where three of AT05's go red and AT06's holds; (M) the suite's TMPDIR export removed by a one-line mutation, where AT06's goes red; (G) `bin/utilz test prez` in the candidate's worktree under an empty TMPDIR of the run's own, green, with nothing left in that TMPDIR and nothing new of Utilz's in `/tmp` or in the system TMPDIR; (U) `Scratch::remove` made silent by a one-line mutation, where (c) goes red; (C) `bin/devbin check all`. Each mutation is restored and its sha checked. K1 (utilz-dc on kovacs, the same bytes): `cargo build` and `cargo test` of the workspace, and `acceptance.sh AT05 AT06` without `--strict`, whose stub checks need no browser, so (a) and (b) run on Linux too; first `findmnt -no OPTIONS /tmp`, since the suite's stubs now run from `/tmp` and a `noexec` mount there would stop them. CI's shellcheck job does not read `*/test/*` (`tests.yml:250`), so a shellcheck 0.9.0 run on `acceptance.sh` would twin nothing, and it is dropped. kovacs has no Chromium (vc's todo 47), so the rest of Ubuntu's acceptance is proven by CI after hv's push.
8. **Versions and CHANGELOG.** prez's binary changes, so prez goes from 2.5.3 to 2.5.4 (`crate/Cargo.toml`, which `prez.yaml` reads). One line under 2.14.2's Fixed (vc's decision 49), added at the landing, which opens `## [2.14.2] - unreleased` if it lands first.
